title: Maximum Vacation Days
summary: Given an n x n matrix representing flights between cities and an n x k matrix representing the maximum vacation days allowed in each city for each week, determine the maximum number of vacation days that can be taken over k weeks.
statement: Given an n x n matrix representing flights between cities and an n x k matrix representing the maximum vacation days allowed in each city for each week, determine the maximum number of vacation days that can be taken over k weeks. You can only travel on the first day of each week, stay beyond the vacation days limit, and count the flight day as vacation in the destination city.
constraints: flights is n by n and days is n by weeks; start in city zero.
Each Monday either stay or take one available directed flight, then collect that destination week’s days.
hints: At each week only the current city and accumulated total matter.
Transition from every reachable city to itself and each flight destination.
Every legal itinerary has one final city per week, so the layered DP considers it once and keeps its best prefix.
editorial: Every legal itinerary has one final city per week, so the layered DP considers it once and keeps its best prefix.

tests.explanation: Choosing reachable cities week by week yields twelve vacation days.
With no flights, every week must be spent in city zero for three total days.
